findings.description: The security group allows inbound TCP port 22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or exploit attempts against the instance.
The egress rule permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, allowing a compromised instance unrestricted outbound communication for data exfiltration or C2.

findings.issue_category: Hardcoded cloud credentials in user data
findings.description: The user_data script exports static AWS access key ID and secret access key values; EC2 user data is readable via the instance metadata service by any process or SSRF on the host, leaking long-lived credentials.
No metadata_options block sets http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains enabled and any SSRF against the host can retrieve instance credentials and the user_data containing secrets.
The instance does not specify root_block_device with encrypted = true, so the root EBS volume may store data at rest unencrypted.
The instance is launched into a subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch enabled and is routed to an internet gateway with a wide-open security group, placing it directly on the public internet.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, so data written to the attached disk is stored unencrypted.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted volume, so the backup data is also stored without encryption at rest.
The VPC flow log bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration, so sensitive network telemetry may be stored unencrypted.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or ACL/policy restrictions are defined for the flow-log bucket, risking public exposure of network traffic logs.
The bucket lacks versioning/MFA delete and force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all flow-log evidence to be deleted without protection, undermining audit log integrity.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP, automatically expanding internet-facing attack surface.

No aws_default_security_group resource restricts the VPC's default security group, leaving it with its default permissive rules available to any resource launched without an explicit group.
